name: memory
description: Durable facts that persist across sessions and are injected into every turn: keep entries compact. Put ALL changes to one target in ONE `operations` call ({action, content?, old_text?}); it is atomic and the char limit is checked on the FINAL result, so remove/patch stale entries and add new ones together. When full, an add is rejected with the entries shown: reissue ONE batch that frees room and adds. The result confirms completion: don't repeat the call. Only facts true for EVERY session (who the user is, stable environment facts, standing conventions); what you learn doing a task (procedures, pitfalls, per-task preferences) belongs in that task's skill via skill_manage. Skip trivial or easily re-discovered facts, raw dumps, task progress, completed-work logs, TODO state. One call writes one tier. note_read must be a call by itself. Details: skill_view hermes-tools-guide

target.description: 'memory' = your notes (environment, conventions, tool quirks, lessons); 'user' = who the user is (name, role, preferences, style).

operations.description: Changes applied atomically against the final char budget; one change = a one-item list.

content.description: Required for add/patch. add: the new entry. patch: the text that replaces old_text (rest of the entry kept).

old_text.description: REQUIRED for patch/remove: text from one entry. patch replaces exactly this span (must occur once there); remove deletes the whole entry.

tier.description: core (default) | project (this git repo, small limit) | archive (no limit, not shown every chat; one-line entries, long text in `note`). Applies to every action, incl. finding the entry for patch/remove/note_read.

tags.description: Up to 8 short labels, for add or patch.

links.description: Up to 8 of 'skill:<name>', 'file:<path>', 'session:<id>', 'memory:<id>', for add or patch.

note.description: Long body (project/archive only), kept in a linked file; add or patch. Read with action note_read + old_text + tier.
